"Owner: free. Pins the call shape of every function published on `window.AISS`, and the rule for changing one.

WHY THIS EXISTS
Adding a parameter to a published function — even a defaulted one — changes how Pro must call it, and Pro cannot notice: no throw, no type complaint, no failing test on either side. `actionState` grew its fifth parameter `rowBlock = null` exactly that way, and nothing anywhere went red. This contract plus its test is the announcement mechanism.

THE PINNED SIGNATURES (free 1.3.2)
  app.apiFetch                     ( path, options = {} )
  app.useAppContext                ()
  app.useToast                     ()
  app.useBackups                   ()
  app.format.formatRelativeTime    ( unixSeconds, nowMs = Date.now() )
  app.format.formatAbsoluteTime    ( unixSeconds )
  app.format.stripScheme           ( url )
  app.format.formatPasscode        ( pin )
  app.format.formatOnOff           ( value )
  app.format.formatBytes           ( bytes )
  app.sync.actionState             ( available, side, statuses, status, rowBlock = null )
  registerComponent                ( slot, component )
  registerFilter                   ( name, callback )

ENFORCEMENT: tests/js/extensions/PublishedSignatures.test.js (free). Four guarantees:
1. Each signature above matches the source declaration, character for character.
2. No function may be published that is not on this list — a new one fails the suite until it is pinned here.
3. Every published function still works detached from its namespace (Pro destructures them), so none may read `this`.
4. None is a bound function.

DO NOT USE Function.length TO CHECK THIS. It counts only parameters before the first
defaulted one, so `actionState` reports 4 both before and after `rowBlock = null` was
added — blind to the exact class of change this contract exists to catch. `Function.toString()`
is no better: Babel rewrites defaults into `arguments.length` checks in the body, and an
async function becomes a `function apiFetch(_x)` trampoline. The test therefore reads the
declaration out of the source file, which is the only place the real signature survives.
Both sides reached this independently — free by measuring the transform, Pro by inspection.

CHANGING A SIGNATURE IS A TWO-STEP RELEASE, AND THE SECOND STEP IS NOT OPTIONAL:
update the pin, then update this contract and message pro. Updating the pin alone
silently reintroduces the failure it was written to prevent.

NOT COVERED HERE, COVERED ELSEWHERE: the published non-function names — `app.sync.PUSH_STATUSES`,
`PULL_STATUSES`, `SYNC_BLOCK_MESSAGES`, and the `components` key set — are pinned as exact
key lists in tests/js/extensions/api.test.js, which also asserts they are frozen copies Pro
cannot mutate. Component props are deliberately outside both: a named prop is additive and
cannot silently change what an existing call means, which is precisely what a positional
parameter does.

RELATED: EXTENSION_API_VERSION is NOT a lever for signature changes. Pro gates registration
on strict equality (`PRO_EXTENSION_API_VERSION === api.extensionApiVersion`), so a bump stops
every Pro registration — Get Pro, the tabs and retention filters, Settings, both host
comparison views, Sync all — until Pro ships a matching build. See updates.pair-lockstep,
which is rationale and not yet built. Consequence recorded 2026-07-27: a published helper is
never deleted merely for being unused. `formatOnOff` has no caller in either plugin and stays,
now with behavioural coverage in tests/js/utils/format.test.js rather than an identity
assertion alone."

"Owner: free. Published 2026-07-27, free 1.3.2, in response to pro task #26. Additive — no EXTENSION_API_VERSION change (and see ui.extension-api-signatures for why a bump is never the answer).

`window.AISS.app.pairing`, all frozen copies, mirroring `app.sync`:

  GATED_OUTCOMES    ['approval-pending', 'otp-required', 'refused']
                    Outcomes that persist until something changes on the peer, so the
                    Settings tab renders them inline rather than in a passing toast.
  POLLED_OUTCOMES   ['approval-pending']
                    Outcomes free re-runs detection for on a timer. `otp-required` and
                    `refused` are excluded DELIBERATELY: neither moves until a human acts
                    on this site, so polling them is a request that can never change
                    anything. Do not add a timer to any other outcome.
  POLL_MS           20000   — drives the interval
  POLL_SECONDS      20      — the figure the disclosure says out loud
                    Both units are published because an override needs each for a
                    different job. Deriving one from the other is how a screen ends up
                    promising a cadence it does not keep.
  OUTCOME_MESSAGES  { outcome: sentence } for all nine outcomes
  OUTCOME_VARIANTS  { outcome: bootstrap variant } for all nine

CONSUME, DO NOT COPY. A map of your own keyed by outcome renders **silence** — not a stale
sentence — the day free adds a tenth outcome, because the lookup misses and yields null.
Layer host-specific rewording ON TOP of OUTCOME_MESSAGES so an unknown outcome falls
through to free's sentence. Pro's three host-worded overrides (HostSettings:35-50, "the
host" where free says "the peer site") are correct and stay: a Pro connector reaching those
three outcomes has a Pro host at the other end, which free cannot assume.

WHY THIS EXISTS: Pro held a frozen copy of GATED_OUTCOMES. It was identical to free's and
entirely unguarded — free could add a fourth and nothing on either side would go red. Pro
raised it against itself during the task-25 override audit.

ENFORCEMENT, free side (tests/js/extensions/api.test.js):
- exact key set on `app.pairing`, and `Object.isFrozen` on the namespace and each list
- published lists are copies, not the constants — `GATED_OUTCOMES.push()` throws and the
  real constant is unchanged
- POLL_MS === POLL_SECONDS * 1000
- **every outcome in GATED_OUTCOMES and POLLED_OUTCOMES has an entry in both
  OUTCOME_MESSAGES and OUTCOME_VARIANTS.** This is the assertion that earns its place, and
  pro proposed it: membership is easy to keep in step, the sentence behind it is what gets
  forgotten. Mutation-verified — adding a gated outcome with no message fails the suite.

Free will not add an outcome to either list without a message, a variant, and a message to
pro on this contract."

"{\"feature\": \"Host mode: a Pro site (the host) accepts an arbitrary number of connected peer sites for comparison and pairwise sync. Peers run plain Free, configured normally: Peer site URL = host URL, shared key = the host's single shared key.\", \"decisions_locked_by_user\": {\"sync_model\": \"Pairwise per-peer only (v1). Each peer column carries today's push/pull/restore semantics against that one peer, one operation at a time, OTP unchanged per pair. No broadcast, no canonical-host model.\", \"otp_on_connect\": \"When the host's OTP toggle is on, a connector proving it knows the host's current rotating connect PIN IS the approval — no OK/Reject click at the host. When OTP is off, the host admin approves each connection via OK/Reject.\", \"key_model\": \"Single host key. Block/delete refuse by registered origin only (soft); host UI must note that rotating the shared key is the hard revocation. No per-peer keys.\", \"free_ui\": \"Free stays single-peer (no host toggle, single Peer URL input). Free gains only dormant connector affordances: pending-approval / otp-required / refused pairing outcomes and a connect-PIN entry that appear only when a Pro host demands them.\"}, \"architecture\": \"All multi-peer state and logic live in Pro (peer registry, approval flow, connect PIN, comparison fan-out, multi-column UI, host-initiated sync via aissp/v1 routes). Free ships an enumerated set of dormant PHP filters + one default-deny peer route + outbound identity headers (contract hostmode.php-hooks / hostmode.identity-headers). Connector-facing traffic keeps using free aiss/v1 routes unchanged — a connector cannot tell a Pro host from a free peer once approved.\", \"connect_flow\": \"1) Connector saves host URL + host key, SPA fires pairing/retest → signed GET /aiss/v1/inventory at host with X-AISS-Origin-Url header. 2) Pro (aiss_serve_inventory filter): blocked origin → WP_Error aiss_connection_refused; unknown origin → back-fetch {origin}/wp-json/aiss/v1/inventory (signed, own transport) and only if that snapshot names the host as ITS peer, store a pending-peer record (name/url/admin_page_url from the back-fetched snapshot, actor from X-AISS-Actor header, display-only) → refuse with aiss_pending_approval (OTP off) or aiss_connect_otp_required (OTP on); approved origin → serve the free snapshot with peer_url overwritten to that peer's registered URL. 3) Approval: OTP off → host admin OK/Reject in Pro Settings UI; OTP on → connector admin enters the host's rotating 6-digit connect PIN, free POSTs signed /aiss/v1/pairing/authorize {pin}, Pro's aiss_pairing_authorize filter verifies (60s rotation, attempt-limited, wrong==expired answer identical) and approves the pending origin. 4) Connector re-tests → gets snapshot naming it → probes → Pro answers probe per-origin (back-fetch the REGISTRY url, never a request-supplied one) → connector pins mutual. From then on it is an ordinary mutual pairing from the connector's view.\", \"sync_flow\": \"Connector-initiated push/pull go through free code paths on both ends; on the host, Pro supplies per-origin pairing verification via aiss_pre_sync_peer_snapshot (live back-fetch of the claimed origin's registry URL; the claimed origin comes from X-AISS-Origin-Url but the fetch target is always the registry entry), aiss_expected_package_origin pins the package URL for receives, and aiss_outbound_peer_url redirects the host's outbound OTP verify/state (and any other signed_post) to the active session's registered peer. Host-initiated push/pull run through Pro's own aissp/v1 routes reusing blessed free PHP classes; use AISS_Sync::acquire_lock()/refresh_lock()/release_lock() (being made public) so free and Pro operations share the one-at-a-time lock. OTP for host-initiated syncs: drive free AISS_Otp::begin_initiator() with the target peer's name/url — the free OtpModal picks the session up via its normal polling on both sites.\", \"delete_vs_block\": \"Delete removes the peer (it may knock again → new pending record). Block is a standing refusal (mirrors free's dismissed-proposal pattern): knocks answer aiss_connection_refused and never create pending records. Both controls borderless icon buttons in the Pro peer list.\", \"limits_v1\": \"Host↔peer pairs are mutual-only (a NAT'd/private connector cannot be back-fetch-verified — unsupported in host mode v1). Host OTP setting is global and must match each peer pairwise to sync, same as today. One OTP handshake and one sync operation at a time, host-wide (free's existing constraints). Column show/hide + reorder persist per admin user (user meta via an aissp route).\"}"

"{\"status\": \"free side landing now — signatures final; wait for the 'free side built' message before live e2e\", \"hooks\": {\"aiss_serve_inventory\": {\"type\": \"filter\", \"signature\": \"apply_filters( 'aiss_serve_inventory', array $snapshot, WP_REST_Request $request )\", \"where\": \"AISS_API::get_inventory(), before rest_ensure_response\", \"returns\": \"array (served as the snapshot) | WP_Error (refusal sent to the requester). Non-array non-WP_Error falls back to the unfiltered snapshot.\", \"pro_use\": \"Host mode: per-origin peer_url echo for approved peers; refusal codes aiss_pending_approval / aiss_connect_otp_required / aiss_connection_refused for pending/blocked/unknown origins (these exact codes — the free connector maps them to pairing outcomes, see hostmode.connector-ux). NEVER put the shared key or any secret in the snapshot.\"}, \"aiss_pre_handle_probe\": {\"type\": \"filter\", \"signature\": \"apply_filters( 'aiss_pre_handle_probe', null, WP_REST_Request $request )\", \"where\": \"AISS_API::pairing_probe(), before AISS_Pairing::handle_probe()\", \"returns\": \"null (free single-peer behavior) | array probe answer e.g. {reached: bool} | WP_Error (refusal).\", \"pro_use\": \"Host mode: back-fetch the claimed origin's REGISTRY url (never an address from the request) and answer reached accordingly; unknown/blocked origins → reached false or WP_Error.\"}, \"aiss_pre_sync_peer_snapshot\": {\"type\": \"filter\", \"signature\": \"apply_filters( 'aiss_pre_sync_peer_snapshot', null, string $entry )\", \"where\": \"AISS_Sync::verify_pairing( $entry ) — $entry is 'initiate' (SPA prepare), 'receive' (peer push arriving), or 'package' (peer pull request). Runs after the local read-only refusal, before the live fetch.\", \"returns\": \"null (free behavior: live-fetch the single configured peer) | array (treated as the verified live peer snapshot — free STILL runs its compatibility checks against it: names-this-site, mode agreement, OTP both-or-neither, peer read_only, zip support; only the is-configured check is skipped since a host has no single peer_url) | WP_Error (refusal).\", \"pro_use\": \"Host mode: resolve X-AISS-Origin-Url → registry entry → live back-fetch that registry URL → return the fetched snapshot. Return WP_Error for unknown/pending/blocked origins.\"}, \"aiss_expected_package_origin\": {\"type\": \"filter\", \"signature\": \"apply_filters( 'aiss_expected_package_origin', string $peer_url )\", \"where\": \"AISS_Sync::validate_package_descriptor() — the URL whose scheme/host/port a package descriptor must match\", \"returns\": \"string base URL\", \"pro_use\": \"During a host-side receive: return the registry URL of the verified origin peer so its package URL pins correctly (host's free peer_url setting is empty).\"}, \"aiss_outbound_peer_url\": {\"type\": \"filter\", \"signature\": \"apply_filters( 'aiss_outbound_peer_url', string $peer_url, string $route )\", \"where\": \"AISS_Remote — target resolution for fetch_peer_snapshot() and every signed_post() (OTP begin/verify/state, receive, package, probe, inventory push, pairing authorize). Applied before the not-configured guard, so a host with an empty stored peer_url can still send.\", \"returns\": \"string base URL of the site to call\", \"pro_use\": \"Host mode: read the active AISS_Otp::get_session() (public) peer_url, validate it against the registry, return the registry URL — this is how the host's OTP verify/state calls reach the right connector. Never return a URL that is not a registry entry.\"}, \"aiss_pairing_authorize\": {\"type\": \"filter\", \"signature\": \"apply_filters( 'aiss_pairing_authorize', null, WP_REST_Request $request )\", \"where\": \"handler of the NEW peer-facing route POST /aiss/v1/pairing/authorize (permission: require_valid_signature; body arg: pin, sanitized by AISS_Otp::sanitize_pin). Default-deny: null → WP_Error aiss_not_host 409.\", \"returns\": \"null (free default: aiss_not_host refusal) | array e.g. {authorized: true} | WP_Error (e.g. wrong/expired PIN — answer wrong and expired identically).\", \"pro_use\": \"Host mode + OTP on: verify the submitted connect PIN (rotate every 60s, attempt-limit like AISS_Otp::MAX_PIN_ATTEMPTS, then approve the pending peer identified by X-AISS-Origin-Url and return {authorized: true}.\"}}, \"blessed_php_classes\": \"Pro PHP may call these free classes directly as a stable surface (breaking changes will be contract-versioned): AISS_Signature::build_headers/sign, AISS_Package::create/validate_zip_root/zip_support/delete_package_file/local_version/resolve_source_dir/find_plugin, AISS_Installer::create_backup/install/restore/require_writable_destination/backup_for/clear_backup, AISS_Otp (begin_initiator/get_session/require_confirmed/session_view/handle_* /mark_running/mark_final/is_enabled/sanitize_pin), AISS_Comparison::compare/summarize, AISS_Inventory::get_snapshot/own_site_url/own_site_name/types/sanitize_items/sanitize_site, AISS_Sync::urls_match/validate_package_descriptor/sanitize_slug/install_from_peer + acquire_lock/refresh_lock/release_lock (being made public — share the one-operation-at-a-time lock with free), AISS_Log::record/classify/state/unknown_state/local_actor/remote_actor/actor_name/site_name, AISS_Remote::pretty_route_endpoint/fallback_route_endpoint/download_package, AISS_Settings::get_shared_key/is_otp_enabled/is_read_only/capability (host key IS free's stored shared_key — do not store a second copy).\"}"

"{\"headers\": {\"X-AISS-Origin-Url\": \"AISS_Inventory::own_site_url() of the sender. Attached to EVERY outbound signed peer request (snapshot fetch and all signed POSTs).\", \"X-AISS-Actor\": \"rawurlencode() of the acting admin's display name (AISS_Log::actor_name()), attached when a logged-in user triggered the call. Receivers must rawurldecode + sanitize_text_field. Display only.\"}, \"trust_model\": \"These headers are NOT signature-bound (deliberately — binding them would break wire compatibility with older free peers, and with a single shared key any key-holder could sign any origin anyway, so binding adds nothing against the realistic adversary). They are routing hints and display data ONLY. Enforcement on the host must never trust them beyond 'a valid key-holder claims to be X': every decision goes through the registry + a live back-fetch of the REGISTRY-stored URL (which must name the host as its peer). A pending record is only created after such a verified back-fetch, so a key-holder cannot spam arbitrary URLs into the pending list. This matches free's existing trust model, where signature alone already grants comparison reads and sync gates rest on live mutual verification + OTP.\", \"compat\": \"Older peers ignore the unknown headers; signature format is unchanged. Free↔free behavior is byte-identical.\"}"

"{\"what_free_ships\": \"Dormant connector-side affordances that only activate against a Pro host. Free↔free pairing is untouched.\", \"peer_error_codes_the_host_must_emit\": {\"aiss_pending_approval\": \"Connection knock recorded, waiting for host admin OK (OTP off). HTTP 403. Free maps it to pairing outcome 'approval-pending'.\", \"aiss_connect_otp_required\": \"Host requires the connect passcode (OTP on). HTTP 403. Free maps it to outcome 'otp-required' and shows a 6-digit PIN input + Authorize control in the Settings pairing panel.\", \"aiss_connection_refused\": \"Origin is blocked or rejected. HTTP 403. Free maps it to outcome 'refused'.\", \"note\": \"Free reads the code from the JSON error body ('code' key) — AISS_Remote now propagates it as 'peer_code' in WP_Error data. Any other code keeps today's 'peer-unreachable' outcome.\"}, \"authorize_flow\": \"The connector's Settings pairing panel, on outcome 'otp-required', shows a PIN input. Submitting fires the existing SPA route POST /aiss/v1/pairing/retest with a NEW optional 'pin' body arg. AISS_Pairing::detect( $pin ) first sends signed POST {host}/aiss/v1/pairing/authorize with body {pin: '123456'} (route constant ROUTE_PAIRING_AUTHORIZE). On WP_Error the SPA surfaces the host's message (wrong/expired PIN). On success detection continues normally: fetch snapshot (now naming this site) → probe → pin mutual.\", \"new_pairing_outcomes\": [{\"outcome\": \"approval-pending\", \"variant\": \"info\"}, {\"outcome\": \"otp-required\", \"variant\": \"info\"}, {\"outcome\": \"refused\", \"variant\": \"danger\"}]}"

    "single-private": "one reachable + one unreachable — one-way pairing",

    "multi-private": "reachable network + unreachable network",

  },

    "import": "import { test, expect, useStack, site, resetStack } from '../lib/fixtures.js'",

    "site": "site(stack, 'hub') -> { name, url, port, container, variant, multisite }",
    "admin": "the `admin` fixture: `const page = await admin(someSite, '#/settings')` returns an authenticated, mounted SPA page. EACH CALL IS A SEPARATE BROWSER CONTEXT — that is what makes two simultaneous admins (the OTP handshake) expressible.",

Pro coverage task open.\",\"stable_api\":{\"begin_initiator\":\"AISS_Otp::begin_initiator( array $item ) : array|WP_Error — returns the session array whose ['id'] is the session id Pro persists as otp_session\",\"require_confirmed\":\"AISS_Otp::require_confirmed( string $session_id, string $type, string $slug ) : true|WP_Error\",\"mark_running\":\"AISS_Otp::mark_running( bool $notify_peer ) : void\",\"mark_final\":\"AISS_Otp::mark_final( bool $success, string $message, bool $notify_peer ) : void\",\"unchanged_by_the_fix\":\"All four signatures, the session id, and the session_view key names (state, enteredHere, enteredThere). Verified: nothing outside AISS_Otp read the stored shape — only session_view() output crosses any boundary.\"},\"what_changed\":{\"storage\":\"entered_here / entered_there moved OUT of the aiss_otp_session transient into aiss_otp_entered_here / aiss_otp_entered_there. Each has exactly one writer (enter_pin locally, handle_verify from the peer), so the shared cell that made the lost update possible no longer exists. Each stores the session id it applies to, not a boolean, so a flag outliving its handshake cannot count toward a later one.\",\"promotion\":\"awaiting -> confirmed is DERIVED on read via effective_state(), not written. A promotion that is never written cannot be lost.\",\"recovery\":\"An awaiting handshake idle beyond AWAITING_IDLE_LIMIT (180s) is superseded rather than refusing new ones. is_abandoned() keys off the EFFECTIVE state, so a confirmed or running session is never superseded.\"},\"the_bug\":{\"what\":\"Two request paths read-modify-wrote one transient and blind-overwrote it. Whichever saved last wiped the other's acknowledgement, so both sites sat at enteredHere=true/enteredThere=false and the handshake never confirmed.\",\"evidence\":\"Flags sampled once a second from both sites' transients during a real handshake. Local control: awaiting(False,False) -> confirmed(True,True). Failing run: both sites frozen at (True,False) for the full 120s. Reproduced on BOTH tiers across runs, so it is a plain race — overlap is the variable, not latency.\",\"regression_test\":\"tests/php/OtpTest.php::test_a_peer_entry_arriving_mid_call_is_not_overwritten. Fires the peer's verification between enter_pin()'s re-read and its write. Verified failing against the committed AISS_Otp with 'the peer entry was overwritten'. The three supersede tests are new-feature tests, NOT regression tests — they assert behaviour with no analogue in the old code.\"},\"SEVERITY_CORRECTION\":{\"v1_said\":\"A deadlocked session jams begin_initiator() for the full SESSION_TTL of 900s; on a host it refuses every connector — a 15-minute whole-host outage.\",\"that_was_wrong\":\"Twice over, both caught by pro and both verified in code by free before being recorded here. (1) OtpModal/index.jsx:406 renders Cancel under { awaiting && ... } — present in exactly the deadlocked state — wired to /sync/otp/cancel -> AISS_Otp::cancel(), which clears both sides. (2) useOtpSession dismissedRef is useRef(new Set()), per page load and never persisted, and poll() runs on mount and re-opens the modal for any active non-final session. So an admin cannot reach the busy refusal without first being shown the stale handshake and its Cancel button.\",\"accurate\":\"The lost update is a real defect: a sync both humans approved could not run. But it is escapable with one click, and supersede-after-idle saves that click rather than averting an outage. It covers only the case where nobody loads the admin page for 180s+, and if nobody is loading the page nobody is syncing either.\",\"lesson_worth_keeping\":\"Both overstatements were plausible, and one of them drove a scope decision put to the human before anyone read the UI layer. Trace the escape hatches before pricing a bug's severity.\"}}"

  "stack_lease": {
    "why": "Both suites share one com.appideas.aiss-e2e label, one port block per topology, and a globalSetup that calls downAll(). A second run does not queue — it destroys the first mid-test, and the victim reports ordinary assertion failures with no hint anything external happened.",

    "ttl": "60 minutes as a backstop; liveness (process.kill(pid, 0)) is the real check. A dead holder is taken over automatically — only a hard kill -9 leaves a file, and even that self-heals on the next run.",
    "acquire_is_ahead_of_downAll": "Deliberate and load-bearing. Every collision either agent hit came through the DESTRUCTIVE path, not the startup path: the damage was never two runs interleaving, it was downAll() deleting a live stack out from under a run already in progress.",
    "validated_live": {
      "when": "v7, this round. FIRST REAL FIRING — every prior confirmation was the regression test.",

      "process_note": "set_status is NOT polled by the other agent.     "the_bug_that_needed_a_second_fix": {
      "what_happened": "v4 guarded globalSetup only. Playwright runs globalTeardown EVEN WHEN globalSetup THREW — including when it threw because another suite holds the lease. Observed for real: free's run printed the refusal and then '[aiss-e2e] removed 3 container(s)', killing a live suite.",
      "fix": "globalTeardown reads the lease first and returns early when it is held by another pid, printing '[aiss-e2e] not tearing down — pid N holds the stack lease.' Only the lease holder may downAll().",

Four cases: foreign live holder (no downAll, lease survives), own lease (downAll once, lease released), no lease (downAll), AISS_E2E_KEEP with own lease (no downAll, lease still released). CONFIRMED to fail on the pre-fix code.",
      "lesson_worth_keeping": "The tests were written around the MECHANISM rather than around the FAILURE. acquire / refuse / stale-takeover / release all passed in isolation and all were real; the defect lived in the path AFTER a refusal, which none of them entered.   "playwright_non_waiting_methods": {
    "THE_RULE": "`isVisible()` and `isHidden()` are the two Playwright state methods that DO NOT AUTO-WAIT. Every other is*() does. In a page object this means a NOT-YET-RENDERED element and an ABSENT-BY-DESIGN element are indistinguishable — both answer false, instantly. Never let `isVisible()` be the first thing a helper does to a freshly-opened page.",
    "what_it_cost": "free's settings().open(card) decided 'is this card already open?' with `await save.isVisible()`. A card that had not rendered yet read exactly like a shut one, so the helper went on to click a disclosure toggle that an always-open card does not have, and burned the full 20s actionTimeout.",
    "the_38ms_trace": "34.410s openAdmin() resolves (it waits for #aiss-admin-app and the tab strip). 34.440s open('sites') finds no -save, clicks the nonexistent -toggle. 34.478s GET /aiss/v1/settings responds and the Settings view swaps LoadingSpinner for the cards. 54.440s timeout. Missed by 38 MILLISECONDS.",
    "why_it_looked_like_flake": "openAdmin() waits for the TAB STRIP, which the shell renders from config before useSettings() has fetched anything. So the window exists on every page open and is only entered by a helper whose FIRST action is a non-waiting read. In the failing spec, alpha's first act is an `expect` (auto-waits, fine) and bravo's is connect() -> open('sites') (does not). One site of two, one spec of 62, on a timing margin — indistinguishable from flake until the trace is read.",
    "SELF_HEALING_VS_FATAL": "For a card WITH a toggle the bug is invisible: the follow-up click auto-waits for the toggle to appear and the card opens anyway, so the wrong decision is silently corrected. It is FATAL only where the recovery does not exist — an always-open card, which has no toggle, ever. This is why it sat undetected: the free Settings tab has two toggle cards and one always-open one.",
    "the_fix": {
      "shape": "await root.getByTestId( testId ).waitFor({state:'visible'});  if ( 0 === await toggle.count() ) return;  if ( await save.isVisible() ) return;  await toggle.click();  await save.waitFor(...)",
      "who": "free found and diagnosed it; PRO proposed this shape and free adopted it verbatim in lib/ui.js. pro applied the same to lib/pro-ui.js settings().open() and columnManager().open().",
      "why_toggle_anchored_beats_card_anchored": "free's first fix only waited for the card root. That rescues an always-open card that HAS a footer (its Save appears, so the isVisible() fast path returns) but leaves a FOOTERLESS always-open card exactly as broken — no toggle to wait for AND no Save to fall back on. pro's aissp-settings-registry is exactly that card. Anchoring on the toggle handles both, and is derived from the component contract rather than from the symptom.",
      "the_component_contract_it_rests_on": "free's SettingsCard: `const open = onToggle ? expanded : true`. A MISSING TOGGLE *IS* THE 'ALWAYS OPEN' SIGNAL. And SettingsCard's own docblock advertises the footerless variant ('Omitting both onSave and onCancel drops the footer entirely, for a group whose contents save themselves'), so a footerless card is an invited configuration in BOTH repos, not a Pro quirk.",
      "count_is_not_racy_here": "The toggle renders in the same React commit as the card, so once the card root is visible the toggle either exists or never will. The count() is only safe AFTER the card-root wait — do not reorder those two.",
      "addressable_while_shut": "SettingsCard puts data-testid={testId} on the Card ROOT, outside the Collapse, so the card is locatable whether open or shut. That is what makes the wait possible; do not move it inside."
    },
    "regression_test": {
      "where": "free tests/js/e2e/settings-card-open.test.js — 5 tests against a fake page/locator, no browser.",
      "why_not_e2e": "The race window is however long GET /settings happens to take. A browser test can only make it deterministic by stalling the response, which proves the fix once but is not a stable guard. The ORDERING is what must hold, and that is assertable directly.",
      "the_gate_was_run": "2 of the 5 fail against the pre-fix helper — 'card with neither toggle nor Save' and 'reads nothing until the card is on screen'. The other 3 pass under BOTH implementations and say so in their own comments: notably the Sites case, which pre-fix survived by luck via the isVisible() fast path. That luck is exactly why this read as flake for so long.",
      "also_proven_in_a_browser_once": "A throwaway spec stalled GET /settings by 4s via context.route, then called open('sites'): RED at the toggle click without the fix, GREEN with it. Deleted after — it exists in this contract, not in the repo. ~25 lines; recreate it if a similar race is ever suspected."
    },
    "generalisation": "Same lesson as the teardown guard and pro's ColumnManager: the defect was in the arrangement no test entered, not in the logic every test exercised. When a helper BRANCHES on element state, ask what that branch does on a screen that has not finished rendering — and what it does for the one configuration nobody renders yet."
  },

  "stack_lease": {
    "why": "Both suites share one com.appideas.aiss-e2e label, one port block per topology, and a globalSetup that calls downAll(). A second run does not queue — it destroys the first mid-test, and the victim reports ordinary assertion failures with no hint anything external happened.",
    "file": "tests/e2e/.stack-lease.json (gitignored) — { pid, owner, takenAt }. `owner` is the Playwright rootDir, so the refusal names which suite is running.",
    "ttl": "60 minutes as a backstop; liveness (process.kill(pid, 0)) is the real check. A dead holder is taken over automatically — only a hard kill -9 leaves a file, and even that self-heals on the next run.",
    "acquire_is_ahead_of_downAll": "Deliberate and load-bearing. Every collision either agent hit came through the DESTRUCTIVE path, not the startup path: the damage was never two runs interleaving, it was downAll() deleting a live stack out from under a run already in progress.",
    "validated_live": {
      "when": "v7. FIRST REAL FIRING — every prior confirmation was the regression test.",
      "what_happened": "pro announced the stack was free, then started a second run in the window before free took it. free announced and started; free's run was refused at globalSetup and logged '[aiss-e2e] not tearing down — pid 47356 holds the stack lease.' pro's five containers were untouched and the run completed 43/43.",
      "why_it_matters": "Under v4 that identical sequence would have destroyed pro's run mid-test and reported it to pro as ordinary assertion failures. The scenario was not contrived for a test — it arose naturally from two agents' messages crossing, which is exactly the shape the lease exists for.",
      "process_note": "set_status is NOT polled by the other agent. Announce a run with send_message, and treat any 'stack is free' as possibly stale by the time it is read — check the lease file AND `docker ps --filter label=com.appideas.aiss-e2e` before believing it, and check whether a lease holder pid is actually alive before treating the lease as stale.",
      "worked_again_in_v8": "free held the stack for three runs while diagnosing the open() race; pro read the notice, fixed pro-ui.js WITHOUT running e2e, and said so explicitly rather than reporting unverified numbers as green. That is the protocol working as intended — the lease stops destruction, the message stops wasted work, and the honesty about what was NOT verified is what makes the handoff usable."
    },
    "the_bug_that_needed_a_second_fix": {
      "what_happened": "v4 guarded globalSetup only. Playwright runs globalTeardown EVEN WHEN globalSetup THREW — including when it threw because another suite holds the lease. So a correctly-refused run went straight to teardown and downAll()'d the containers of the run it had just declined to disturb. Observed for real: free's run printed the refusal and then '[aiss-e2e] removed 3 container(s)', killing a live suite.",
      "fix": "globalTeardown reads the lease first and returns early when it is held by another pid, printing '[aiss-e2e] not tearing down — pid N holds the stack lease.' Only the lease holder may downAll().",
      "regression_test": "free tests/js/e2e/teardown-guard.test.js. Mocks stack.js so downAll is a spy and stage.js so E2E_ROOT (hence the lease path) lands in a temp dir — a unit test can never touch a real suite's lease. Four cases: foreign live holder (no downAll, lease survives), own lease (downAll once, lease released), no lease (downAll), AISS_E2E_KEEP with own lease (no downAll, lease still released). CONFIRMED to fail on the pre-fix code.",
      "lesson_worth_keeping": "The tests were written around the MECHANISM rather than around the FAILURE. acquire / refuse / stale-takeover / release all passed in isolation and all were real; the defect lived in the path AFTER a refusal, which none of them entered. Same shape as pro's ColumnManager bug, and now the same shape as the open() race. When a guard refuses something, test what still runs after the refusal."
    },
    "what_the_lease_cannot_cover": "Leftover containers are NOT proof of a live run. A suite that exited leaving containers up (AISS_E2E_KEEP, or an interrupted teardown) has no process and no lease, so the next globalSetup will remove them with no opt-out — correctly, since by then nothing owns them. Announcing on this channel stays the only mechanism for a deliberately-kept stack.",
    "escape_hatch": "`npm run stack:lease -- release` (and `-- status`). `npm run status` shows the holder. `npm run down -- --all` warns and pauses 5s if a suite is live — a warning, not a block, so a wedged stack always has a way out. NEVER release another agent's lease unless its pid is genuinely dead.",
    "social_protocol_still_applies": "The lease stops the destruction, not the waiting. Still send_message before starting a long run."
  },

    "THE_RULE": "`isVisible()` and `isHidden()` are the two Playwright state methods that DO NOT AUTO-WAIT. Every other is*() does. In a page object this means a NOT-YET-RENDERED element and an ABSENT-BY-DESIGN element are indistinguishable — both answer false, instantly. Never let `isVisible()` be the first thing a helper does to a freshly-opened page.",
    "what_it_cost": "free's settings().open(card) decided 'is this card already open?' with `await save.isVisible()`. A card that had not rendered yet read exactly like a shut one, so the helper went on to click a disclosure toggle that an always-open card does not have, and burned the full 20s actionTimeout.",
    "the_38ms_trace": "34.410s openAdmin() resolves (it waits for #aiss-admin-app and the tab strip). 34.440s open('sites') finds no -save, clicks the nonexistent -toggle. 34.478s GET /aiss/v1/settings responds and the Settings view swaps LoadingSpinner for the cards. 54.440s timeout. Missed by 38 MILLISECONDS.",
    "why_it_looked_like_flake": "openAdmin() waits for the TAB STRIP, which the shell renders from config before useSettings() has fetched anything. So the window exists on every page open and is only entered by a helper whose FIRST action is a non-waiting read. In the failing spec, alpha's first act is an `expect` (auto-waits, fine) and bravo's is connect() -> open('sites') (does not). One site of two, one spec of 62, on a timing margin — indistinguishable from flake until the trace is read.",
    "SELF_HEALING_VS_FATAL": "For a card WITH a toggle the bug is invisible: the follow-up click auto-waits for the toggle to appear and the card opens anyway, so the wrong decision is silently corrected. It is FATAL only where the recovery does not exist — an always-open card, which has no toggle, ever. This is why it sat undetected: the free Settings tab has two toggle cards and one always-open one.",
    "the_fix": {
      "shape": "await root.getByTestId( testId ).waitFor({state:'visible'});  if ( 0 === await toggle.count() ) return;  if ( await save.isVisible() ) return;  await toggle.click();  await save.waitFor(...)",
      "who": "free found and diagnosed it; PRO proposed this shape and free adopted it verbatim in lib/ui.js. pro applied the same to lib/pro-ui.js settings().open() and columnManager().open().",
      "why_toggle_anchored_beats_card_anchored": "free's first fix only waited for the card root. That rescues an always-open card that HAS a footer (its Save appears, so the isVisible() fast path returns) but leaves a FOOTERLESS always-open card exactly as broken — no toggle to wait for AND no Save to fall back on. pro's aissp-settings-registry is exactly that card. Anchoring on the toggle handles both, and is derived from the component contract rather than from the symptom. MEASURED CONFIRMATION: registry and sites fail IDENTICALLY pre-fix, so the footer is irrelevant to the failure — the missing toggle is the whole cause.",
      "the_component_contract_it_rests_on": "free's SettingsCard: `const open = onToggle ? expanded : true`. A MISSING TOGGLE *IS* THE 'ALWAYS OPEN' SIGNAL. And SettingsCard's own docblock advertises the footerless variant ('Omitting both onSave and onCancel drops the footer entirely, for a group whose contents save themselves'), so a footerless card is an invited configuration in BOTH repos, not a Pro quirk.",

  "stack_lease": {
    "why": "Both suites share one com.appideas.aiss-e2e label, one port block per topology, and a globalSetup that calls downAll(). A second run does not queue — it destroys the first mid-test, and the victim reports ordinary assertion failures with no hint anything external happened.",
    "file": "tests/e2e/.stack-lease.json (gitignored) — { pid, owner, takenAt }. `owner` is the Playwright rootDir, so the refusal names which suite is running.",
    "ttl": "60 minutes as a backstop; liveness (process.kill(pid, 0)) is the real check. A dead holder is taken over automatically — only a hard kill -9 leaves a file, and even that self-heals on the next run.",
    "acquire_is_ahead_of_downAll": "Deliberate and load-bearing. Every collision either agent hit came through the DESTRUCTIVE path, not the startup path: the damage was never two runs interleaving, it was downAll() deleting a live stack out from under a run already in progress.",
    "validated_live": {
      "when": "v7. FIRST REAL FIRING — every prior confirmation was the regression test.",
      "what_happened": "pro announced the stack was free, then started a second run in the window before free took it. free announced and started; free's run was refused at globalSetup and logged '[aiss-e2e] not tearing down — pid 47356 holds the stack lease.' pro's five containers were untouched and the run completed.",
      "why_it_matters": "Under v4 that identical sequence would have destroyed pro's run mid-test and reported it to pro as ordinary assertion failures. The scenario was not contrived for a test — it arose naturally from two agents' messages crossing, which is exactly the shape the lease exists for.",
      "process_note": "set_status is NOT polled by the other agent. Announce a run with send_message, and treat any 'stack is free' as possibly stale by the time it is read — check the lease file AND `docker ps --filter label=com.appideas.aiss-e2e` before believing it, and check whether a lease holder pid is actually alive before treating the lease as stale.",
      "the_v8_v9_handoff_is_the_model": "free held the stack for four runs while diagnosing the open() race; pro read the notice, fixed pro-ui.js WITHOUT running e2e, SAID SO EXPLICITLY rather than reporting unverified numbers as green, and used the waiting time on a headless harness that needs no stack. free posted an explicit all-clear having verified containers AND lease AND ngrok by hand; pro took the stack, announced it, ran 47/47, released, and verified 0 containers themselves rather than trusting the teardown line. Nothing was destroyed and nothing was blocked. Copy this sequence."
    },
    "the_bug_that_needed_a_second_fix": {
      "what_happened": "v4 guarded globalSetup only. Playwright runs globalTeardown EVEN WHEN globalSetup THREW — including when it threw because another suite holds the lease. So a correctly-refused run went straight to teardown and downAll()'d the containers of the run it had just declined to disturb. Observed for real: free's run printed the refusal and then '[aiss-e2e] removed 3 container(s)', killing a live suite.",
      "fix": "globalTeardown reads the lease first and returns early when it is held by another pid, printing '[aiss-e2e] not tearing down — pid N holds the stack lease.' Only the lease holder may downAll().",
      "regression_test": "free tests/js/e2e/teardown-guard.test.js. Mocks stack.js so downAll is a spy and stage.js so E2E_ROOT (hence the lease path) lands in a temp dir — a unit test can never touch a real suite's lease. Four cases: foreign live holder (no downAll, lease survives), own lease (downAll once, lease released), no lease (downAll), AISS_E2E_KEEP with own lease (no downAll, lease still released). CONFIRMED to fail on the pre-fix code.",
      "lesson_worth_keeping": "The tests were written around the MECHANISM rather than around the FAILURE. acquire / refuse / stale-takeover / release all passed in isolation and all were real; the defect lived in the path AFTER a refusal, which none of them entered. Same shape as pro's ColumnManager bug, and now the same shape as the open() race. When a guard refuses something, test what still runs after the refusal."
    },
    "what_the_lease_cannot_cover": "Leftover containers are NOT proof of a live run. A suite that exited leaving containers up (AISS_E2E_KEEP, or an interrupted teardown) has no process and no lease, so the next globalSetup will remove them with no opt-out — correctly, since by then nothing owns them. Announcing on this channel stays the only mechanism for a deliberately-kept stack.",
    "escape_hatch": "`npm run stack:lease -- release` (and `-- status`). `npm run status` shows the holder. `npm run down -- --all` warns and pauses 5s if a suite is live — a warning, not a block, so a wedged stack always has a way out. NEVER release another agent's lease unless its pid is genuinely dead.",
    "social_protocol_still_applies": "The lease stops the destruction, not the waiting. Still send_message before starting a long run."
  },

"{
  "version": 2,
  "owner": "free",
  "status": "CORRECTED. v1 got the diagnostic fact right and the CONCLUSION wrong. No code changed in either plugin — that part stands.",

  "WHAT_CHANGED_IN_v2": "v1 said the failure was a rare dropped SYN on the hairpin path and told you to re-run. It reproduced on the very next run, so 'rare' was wrong. Further runs showed the real driver is HOST RESOURCE STARVATION, and the two different symptoms are one cause. The connect-cap FACT below is verified and still worth knowing; the story around it is rewritten.",

  "STILL_TRUE_the_diagnostic_fact": {
    "THE_RULE": "A cURL 28 reporting `after 100xx ms` is NEVER one of the configured budgets expiring. It is the TCP CONNECT CAP, a hard 10 seconds that nothing in either plugin sets.",
    "chain": "WP_Http::request() builds the Requests options with only `timeout` (class-wp-http.php ~336) and NEVER sets `connect_timeout` — grep it, count is 0. Requests' default stands: `'connect_timeout' => 10` (Requests/src/Requests.php:114). The cURL transport makes it CURLOPT_CONNECTTIMEOUT_MS = 10000 (Transport/Curl.php:437-440).",
    "consequence": "AISS_Remote's 15s/90s/180s/300s budgets govern the REQUEST only. All four sit behind ONE 10-second handshake cap.",
    "use_it_as": "Match the elapsed time to 10s BEFORE theorising about slow packaging. 10s means the handshake; none of our timeouts is involved."
  },

  "STILL_TRUE_overran_vs_never_arrived": {
    "how": "Serving `sync/package` or `sync/receive` makes the PEER call BACK to the initiator for verify_pairing. So a request the peer really handled ALWAYS leaves a line in the PEER's log. No line there = it never arrived and the peer's PHP never ran.",
    "why_it_matters": "These two demand opposite investigations and the httplog attachments already separate them for free."
  },

  "THE_ACTUAL_CAUSE": {
    "verdict": "A starved host stalls the Docker VM for seconds at a time, and the stall surfaces as whatever request happened to be in flight. Two failures one run apart looked like two unrelated bugs and were one.",
    "symptom_1": "sync/package CONNECT timed out at 10005ms, while the GET /inventory immediately before it and immediately after — same host, same port — both returned 200.",
    "symptom_2": "alpha served ONE admin.php for ~56 seconds (matching 56s hole in its outbound log), so page.waitForSelector('#aiss-admin-app') blew its 30s budget. The failure screenshot shows the SPA FULLY MOUNTED — it arrived, just far too late.",
    "why_it_looked_positional": "Same test failed both times, so it read as state left by the theme sync before it. IT IS NOT. That test passes IN ISOLATION in 5.5s, passes PAIRED with the theme sync, and the whole spec file then passed 7/7 with that test at 4.3s.",
    "the_measurement": "Failing run: load average (5 min, 10 CPUs) 18.74, that test 59.7s and failed. Passing run: load 4.32, same test 4.3s. Host at ~57 MB FREE RAM, 90% of swap consumed (12.9 of 14.3 GB), 7.5M pageouts, 26 days uptime. Docker VM holds only 3.83 GiB.",
    "eliminated_by_direct_evidence_not_argument": [
      "Apache worker exhaustion — MaxRequestWorkers is 150, MaxConnectionsPerChild 0.",
      "wp-cli / resetFixtures contention — Docker's backend log shows ZERO ContainerExecCliLinux events across the whole failure window; the harness was idle apart from the browser.",
      "Browser-context leak across tests — the `admin` fixture closes every context it opened in its teardown loop.",
      "State left by the theme sync — the pair (theme sync + failing test) passes together."
    ]
  },

  "WHAT_TO_DO": "When this suite fails on timing, check `uptime`, `sysctl vm.swapusage` and `vm_stat` BEFORE reading a trace, and re-run on a quiet machine. A stalled VM is not a product bug and not a harness bug.",

  "DO_NOT": [
    "Do not add retries. That converts a starved machine into a slow green run and hides the next real regression. The e2e-harness skill has said so since httplog landed and it is still right.",
    "Do not raise the connect timeout in AISS_Remote to 'fix' this — it would not have helped either failure, it is a production behaviour change for every user, and it is in security-sensitive outbound code. Flagged to the human as a product question; code left alone.",
    "Do not add a product-side retry: a WP_Error cannot reliably separate 'never connected' from 'sent, no response', and retrying a sync/receive in the second case would re-install."
  ],

  "free_side_record": "free .claude/skills/e2e-harness/SKILL.md — '~10s elapsed is never the budget' and 'Before blaming the suite, measure the host'."
}"

An overlay outside the mount matches NONE of the bundled CSS — it is bare unstyled text over the page, which is glaring, and is already the first thing free's wp-admin-screenshot skill says about overlays. So the coupling is real and worth recording, but it cannot regress unnoticed: a tooltip that loses this rule has also lost its entire appearance. Documentation is the right weight of response; a dedicated guard is not warranted.\", \"why_a_bigger_offset_is_not_the_fix\": \"Considered and rejected on the measurement. react-bootstrap already applies its `[0, 6]` tooltip offset correctly (Tooltip.TOOLTIP_OFFSET, 2.10.10) — the geometry is right when nothing is moving. A larger offset only shrinks the window in which a transient displacement overlaps; a 14px shift still overlaps. Removing the tooltip from hit-testing removes the feedback path itself.\", \"how_to_re_verify\": \"Do not trust a Jest test — the jsdom test passes with the JS half alone, because jsdom has no layout and therefore no spurious mouseout. Browser only. Hover the control, click it WITHOUT moving the pointer, log mouseout/mouseover on the trigger for ~1s. Any oscillation is the regression. Run it as a counter-run (override the rule, confirm the loop returns) or a green result proves nothing. See free's `wp-admin-screenshot` skill for the authenticated-session setup.\"}"

"Owner: free. Pins the call shape of every function published on `window.AISS`, and the rule for changing one.

WHY THIS EXISTS
Adding a parameter to a published function — even a defaulted one — changes how Pro must call it, and Pro cannot notice: no throw, no type complaint, no failing test on either side. `actionState` grew its fifth parameter `rowBlock = null` exactly that way, and nothing anywhere went red. This contract plus its test is the announcement mechanism.

THE PINNED SIGNATURES (free 1.3.2)
  app.apiFetch                     ( path, options = {} )
  app.useAppContext                ()
  app.useToast                     ()
  app.useBackups                   ()
  app.format.formatRelativeTime    ( unixSeconds, nowMs = Date.now() )
  app.format.formatAbsoluteTime    ( unixSeconds )
  app.format.stripScheme           ( url )
  app.format.formatPasscode        ( pin )
  app.format.formatOnOff           ( value )
  app.format.formatBytes           ( bytes )
  app.sync.actionState             ( available, side, statuses, status, rowBlock = null )
  registerComponent                ( slot, component )
  registerFilter                   ( name, callback )

ENFORCEMENT: tests/js/extensions/PublishedSignatures.test.js (free). Four guarantees:
1. Each signature above matches the source declaration, character for character.
2. No function may be published that is not on this list — a new one fails the suite until it is pinned here.
3. Every published function still works detached from its namespace (Pro destructures them), so none may read `this`.
4. None is a bound function.

DO NOT USE Function.length TO CHECK THIS. It counts only parameters before the first
defaulted one, so `actionState` reports 4 both before and after `rowBlock = null` was
added — blind to the exact class of change this contract exists to catch. `Function.toString()`
is no better: Babel rewrites defaults into `arguments.length` checks in the body, and an
async function becomes a `function apiFetch(_x)` trampoline. The test therefore reads the
declaration out of the source file, which is the only place the real signature survives.
Both sides reached this independently — free by measuring the transform, Pro by inspection.

CHANGING A SIGNATURE IS A TWO-STEP RELEASE, AND THE SECOND STEP IS NOT OPTIONAL:
update the pin, then update this contract and message pro. Updating the pin alone
silently reintroduces the failure it was written to prevent.

NOT COVERED HERE, COVERED ELSEWHERE: the published non-function names — `app.sync.PUSH_STATUSES`,
`PULL_STATUSES`, `SYNC_BLOCK_MESSAGES`, and the `components` key set — are pinned as exact
key lists in tests/js/extensions/api.test.js, which also asserts they are frozen copies Pro
cannot mutate. Component props are deliberately outside both: a named prop is additive and
cannot silently change what an existing call means, which is precisely what a positional
parameter does.

RELATED: EXTENSION_API_VERSION is NOT a lever for signature changes. Pro gates registration
on strict equality (`PRO_EXTENSION_API_VERSION === api.extensionApiVersion`), so a bump stops
every Pro registration — Get Pro, the tabs and retention filters, Settings, both host
comparison views, Sync all — until Pro ships a matching build. See updates.pair-lockstep,
which is rationale and not yet built. Consequence recorded 2026-07-27: a published helper is
never deleted merely for being unused. `formatOnOff` has no caller in either plugin and stays,
now with behavioural coverage in tests/js/utils/format.test.js rather than an identity
assertion alone."

`window.AISS.app.pairing`, all frozen copies, mirroring `app.sync`:

  GATED_OUTCOMES    ['approval-pending', 'otp-required', 'refused']
                    Outcomes that persist until something changes on the peer, so the
                    Settings tab renders them inline rather than in a passing toast.
  POLLED_OUTCOMES   ['approval-pending']
                    Outcomes free re-runs detection for on a timer. `otp-required` and
                    `refused` are excluded DELIBERATELY: neither moves until a human acts
                    on this site, so polling them is a request that can never change
                    anything. Do not add a timer to any other outcome.
  POLL_MS           20000   — drives the interval
  POLL_SECONDS      20      — the figure the disclosure says out loud
                    Both units are published because an override needs each for a
                    different job. Deriving one from the other is how a screen ends up
                    promising a cadence it does not keep.
  OUTCOME_MESSAGES  { outcome: sentence } for all nine outcomes
  OUTCOME_VARIANTS  { outcome: bootstrap variant } for all nine

CONSUME, DO NOT COPY. A map of your own keyed by outcome renders **silence** — not a stale
sentence — the day free adds a tenth outcome, because the lookup misses and yields null.
Layer host-specific rewording ON TOP of OUTCOME_MESSAGES so an unknown outcome falls
through to free's sentence. Pro's three host-worded overrides (HostSettings:35-50, "the
host" where free says "the peer site") are correct and stay: a Pro connector reaching those
three outcomes has a Pro host at the other end, which free cannot assume.

WHY THIS EXISTS: Pro held a frozen copy of GATED_OUTCOMES. It was identical to free's and
entirely unguarded — free could add a fourth and nothing on either side would go red. Pro
raised it against itself during the task-25 override audit.

ENFORCEMENT, free side (tests/js/extensions/api.test.js):
- exact key set on `app.pairing`, and `Object.isFrozen` on the namespace and each list
- published lists are copies, not the constants — `GATED_OUTCOMES.push()` throws and the
  real constant is unchanged
- POLL_MS === POLL_SECONDS * 1000
- **every outcome in GATED_OUTCOMES and POLLED_OUTCOMES has an entry in both
  OUTCOME_MESSAGES and OUTCOME_VARIANTS.** This is the assertion that earns its place, and
  pro proposed it: membership is easy to keep in step, the sentence behind it is what gets
  forgotten. Mutation-verified — adding a gated outcome with no message fails the suite.

Free will not add an outcome to either list without a message, a variant, and a message to
pro on this contract."

  "the_product_in_one_paragraph": "APPideas Site Syncinator connects two WordPress sites so their installed plugins and themes can be compared and synced — version differences and presence differences (installed on one site but not the other). It is wp-admin only; there is no public-facing frontend to screenshot except the admin screen itself. Each site reaches the other over the WordPress REST API, authenticated by an HMAC-SHA256 signature over a shared key. Comparison needs only the shared key; syncing additionally requires the pairing to be MUTUAL — each site's configured peer URL must name the other. The admin UI is one screen with five tabs: Plugins, Themes, Log, Settings, Get PRO.",

  "who_it_is_for": "Anyone maintaining more than one WordPress site who currently reconciles plugin and theme versions by opening two admin screens side by side: agencies, developers running staging alongside production, and anyone with a local dev site that must track a live one.",

tasks.title: Pro launch overrides: hide the Get Pro tab + extended log retention
tasks.body:
Free is shipping (landing now, this branch): (1) a "Get Pro" tab after Settings at route /get-pro with new slot view:get-pro, placeholder content only; (2) an upsell entry closing the free log-retention dropdown ({ value: 'get-pro', label: 'Get more options in Pro' }) that navigates to #/get-pro instead of saving.

Pro work, per contracts ui.get-pro-tab, ui.log-retention-upsell, settings.log-retention-choices (read them — they are the spec):
1. tabs filter: remove the /get-pro tab. Also registerComponent('view:get-pro', component rendering null) so direct #/get-pro links show an empty panel. Keep the route (do not remove via routes filter).
2. logRetentionOptions filter: return the full 8-entry Pro list (Disable, 1 hour, 12 hours, 1 day, 7 days, 30 days, 90 days, Forever) and drop the free upsell sentinel (filter out non-numeric values).
3. PHP aiss_log_retention_choices filter: append [3600, 43200, 86400, 2592000, 7776000, 315360000] so the server accepts the new values (0 and 604800 are free built-ins).

Test on your side: Jest against a stubbed window.AISS (assert your callbacks drop the sentinel, never mutate input, return new arrays) + PHPUnit for the PHP filter, per docs/pro-plugin-agent-brief.md "Testing expectations". For live e2e on the Docker site, wait for my "free side built" message — the free bundle with the new surface isn't built yet. extensionApiVersion stays 1 (additive change).
tasks.note: Built in Pro 0.2.0 (branch develop, uncommitted — human commits). New extension bundle app/dist/extension.js (webpack.extension.config.js, externals → window.AISS.vendor, guards extensionApiVersion === 1): tabs filter drops the /get-pro tab; view:get-pro overridden with a null-rendering BlankView (route kept); logRetentionOptions returns the full 8-entry Pro list, dropping non-numeric values (upsell sentinel). PHP: aiss_log_retention_choices appends [3600, 43200, 86400, 2592000, 7776000, 315360000] (AISSP_Settings::add_log_retention_choices); enqueue via aiss_admin_enqueue_assets with the handed-back handle as dep. Jest (stubbed window.AISS: no-mutation + new-array + sentinel-drop asserted) + PHPUnit (enqueue deps, additive int filter) — 27 JS / 44 PHP tests green, lint clean. Awaiting your "free side built" message for live e2e on the Docker site.

tasks.title: Host mode: multi-peer compare + pairwise sync (Pro engine + UI)
tasks.body:
Read contracts hostmode.design, hostmode.php-hooks, hostmode.identity-headers, hostmode.connector-ux, ui.components-namespace first — they are the spec, and the user has locked the four design decisions recorded in hostmode.design (pairwise sync only; connect-PIN replaces OK/Reject when OTP on; single host key with soft block + rotate-key note; free stays single-peer).

Pro deliverables:

1. HOST MODE CORE (PHP)
   - "Host mode" toggle (Pro setting). When on, hook all six free filters per hostmode.php-hooks. When off, register nothing — a Pro site without host mode behaves exactly like free.
   - Peer registry (one Pro option): entries {url, name, admin_page_url, actor, status: pending|approved|blocked, added_at, last_seen}. Keyed by normalized URL (use AISS_Sync::urls_match semantics).
   - Knock handling in aiss_serve_inventory: back-fetch-verify BEFORE creating a pending record (the back-fetched snapshot must name the host as its peer); emit the three exact refusal codes from hostmode.connector-ux.
   - Connect PIN (host-side, when OTP on): 6 digits, 60s rotation, attempt-limited, wrong==expired identical answer — mirror AISS_Otp's discipline. Verified in aiss_pairing_authorize; success approves the pending origin. PIN displayed only in the manage_options-gated Pro UI, never in any peer-facing payload.
   - Per-origin sync verification via aiss_pre_sync_peer_snapshot / aiss_expected_package_origin / aiss_outbound_peer_url per the contract. Never trust X-AISS-Origin-Url beyond registry lookup; all fetches go to registry URLs.

2. AISSP/V1 ROUTES (all with real permission_callbacks, manage_options via AISS_Settings::capability())
   - peers: list / approve / reject / delete / block / unblock.
   - comparison/{type}: fan-out — per-peer signed snapshot fetch (own transport reusing AISS_Signature::build_headers + AISS_Remote endpoint builders, per-peer cache transients honoring cache_ttl), diff each against local via AISS_Comparison::compare, return per-peer columns + per-peer sync availability (reuse free's pairwise rules: mode mutual, OTP both-or-neither, read_only, zip support).
   - sync prepare/execute/restore with a peer parameter: reuse blessed free classes (AISS_Package, AISS_Installer, AISS_Otp, AISS_Sync::install_from_peer/validate_package_descriptor, AISS_Log) and share free's one-at-a-time lock via AISS_Sync::acquire_lock/refresh_lock/release_lock (public as of this free release). OTP host-initiated: drive AISS_Otp::begin_initiator with the target peer's name/url — free's OtpModal picks it up by polling on both ends; your aiss_outbound_peer_url callback routes the OTP begin/verify/state to that peer.
   - Log every install/push/restore through AISS_Log::record with the peer's display name as target site.

3. UI (view overrides via window.AISS)
   - view:settings, host mode ON: host toggle; peer list replacing the Peer URL input (approved/pending/blocked sections; borderless icon buttons — delete + block, unblock for blocked; OK/Reject on pending cards when OTP off; the rotating connect PIN with OtpCountdown when OTP on); shared-key display with the "rotating the key is the hard revocation" note. Host mode OFF: render the free-equivalent settings via your existing override or don't register the override.
   - view:plugins / view:themes, host mode ON: multi-column comparison — one column per approved peer + local; per-cell pairwise status (reuse STATUS_* semantics); per-peer-column sync/restore controls (SyncActions); column show/hide + drag-reorder, persisted per admin user (user meta via an aissp route). Use window.AISS.components primitives per ui.components-namespace. With 0-1 peers keep the table sensible (1 peer ≈ free layout).
   - Read config through app.useAppContext + your aiss_admin_config namespace ('pro'); never window.AISSConfig.

4. TESTS: Jest (stubbed window.AISS + your views/filters; no-mutation discipline) + PHPUnit/Brain-Monkey (registry transitions incl. block-is-sticky, knock handling incl. back-fetch-verify refusals, PIN rotation/attempts, per-origin verification callbacks, route permissions). Live e2e on the Docker site AFTER my "free side built" message: free connector site ↔ Pro host — full knock → approve (both OTP paths) → multi-column compare → pairwise push+pull+restore → block/delete behavior.

Free side is landing in parallel (filters, /pairing/authorize route, identity headers, connector UX, components namespace). Anything ambiguous or missing in the surface: message me — do not work around the contract. extensionApiVersion stays 1.
tasks.note: Host mode shipped in Pro 0.3.0 (develop working tree, uncommitted per repo policy). All four deliverables built and verified: PHP core (peer registry, connect PIN, six filter callbacks, host sync engine, transport), aissp/v1 routes (all capability-gated), extension UI (settings override with peer sections + PIN card, multi-column comparison with per-peer SyncActions and column prefs), tests (111 PHPUnit + 40 Jest, lint clean). Live e2e against a real second-container connector passed the full matrix: knock/back-fetch-verify, both approval paths (OK + connect PIN via /pairing/authorize), multi-column compare, UI pull/restore/push, OTP-gated sync with session-routed verify calls, block/unblock. Details in message #10; e2e recipe recorded in the Pro host-mode-e2e skill.

tasks.title: Host-mode Settings panel: toasts not sticky alerts, drop a sentence, swap toggles, show THIS SITE url
tasks.body:
Four human-reported changes in Pro's view:settings override.

1. The two yellow warnings that appear when Host mode is on but unconfigured ("Host mode needs the connection switched on below…" and "Set a shared key below…") do not clear after the admin fixes and saves the settings — they persist until reload. The human's fix, verbatim: use Toasts instead, "then we don't have to think about this." Use window.AISS.app.useToast() so they match free's toasts; fire on the state transition, not on every render.

2. Delete this sentence from the Host mode description: "Connecting sites run the free plugin, pointed at this site's URL with this site's shared key."

3. Swap the toggle order: "Allow connections" must come FIRST, then "Host mode". (Free's own Settings already leads with Allow connections.)

4. With Host mode on there is no way to see or copy this site's own URL — the connectors need it. Render the same "THIS SITE <url> [copy]" row free shows under its Peer site URL field. Free is extracting it as components/ThisSiteUrl and exposing it on window.AISS.components in 1.4.0 (contract ui.components-namespace v3): `<ThisSiteUrl url={ siteUrl } />`, url from app.useAppContext(). Do not rebuild it — gate on components.ThisSiteUrl existing if you want a 1.3.0 fallback.
tasks.note: All four done in Pro 0.4.0 (develop working tree, uncommitted). (1) Both sticky yellow Alerts are gone; new controllers/useHostRequirementToasts.js fires them through app.useToast() as `warning` toasts, keyed on a signature of the unmet prerequisites held in a ref — so they announce on the transition into an unmet state, never on every render, do not re-fire on the 25s peer poll, and simply stop once the admin fixes and saves (re-firing if a prerequisite is broken again). (2) The "Connecting sites run the free plugin…" sentence is deleted from the Host mode helpText. (3) Allow connections now renders first, Host mode second. (4) New components/ThisSiteUrl renders free's components.ThisSiteUrl verbatim when the bundle publishes it and falls back to its own equivalent row otherwise, so a 1.3.0 free still shows the address; it is rendered under the Host mode toggle when host mode is on, and it also replaced Pro's old hand-written "This site: <url>" row under the Peer URL field so both paths are now the same component. url comes from app.useAppContext().siteUrl as specified (Pro no longer reads host.data.siteUrl for this). Tests: tests/js/extension/useHostRequirementToasts.test.jsx (announce-once, silent-when-met, re-announce-after-regression, silent while off/loading) and tests/js/extension/ThisSiteUrl.test.jsx (free component preferred, fallback row + copy button, renders nothing without a URL or surface). Jest 60 green, PHPUnit 111 green, lint clean.

tasks.title: Connected Sites list: Bootstrap icons only — trash, lock/unlock
tasks.body:
Human-reported on the host-mode Connected Sites list, plus a standing rule.

1. The delete control must use a proper trash icon, not a text glyph — components.Icon key `trash` (verbatim bi-trash) via components.IconButton.

2. Block/unblock must use the Lock and Unlock icons. Mapping the human specified: an UNBLOCKED peer shows `unlock` ("unblocked — click to block"); a BLOCKED peer shows `lock` (click to unblock). Free 1.4.0 replaces the old `block`/`unblock` glyph keys with `lock` and `unlock` (verbatim bi-lock / bi-unlock) — the old keys are gone, so update in step with free's 1.4.0 bundle or your buttons render empty. Free also adds `pending` (bi-hourglass-split) if you need a waiting marker. Contract ui.components-namespace v3.
